title: RESTORING THE BROKEN MINDS OF THE DAUGHTERS OF ZION

sense.text:
“And, lo, thou art unto them as a very lovely song.” That is how many of our people look at this truth. Every Sabbath they log on, and they love hearing the word of God.

“Of one that hath a pleasant voice, and can play well on an instrument.” The instrument is the Bible. The Bishops and the Deacons can break down the scriptures, and they play well on that instrument; the people sit and enjoy watching it done.

“For they hear thy words, but they do them not.” That is a lot of brothers and sisters. They hear the scriptures brought out and don't want to do what is taught, because what is taught is right, and it cuts against the way our people were trained to think. Everything we were taught here in Babylon is wrong. The sisters' state of mind has to change, because this nation cannot be built until it does.

“And when this cometh to pass, (lo, it will come,) then shall they know that a prophet hath been among them.” People will come and sit as if they want to learn, and do nothing that is said. But the Deacons and the Bishops are prophets, and when the things they speak of come to pass, the people will know a prophet was among them.

Meanwhile some go online, get into their emotions and distort what was said. It was never taught that postpartum is not real: postpartum is in the Bible, with the woman's sickness and sorrows and the days of her purification after she gives birth. What was taught is not to take on Esau's label of depression, because there is psychological warfare behind his terms. Use what the Bible says instead.

“My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.” We are a destroyed people, and the knowledge we lack is the laws of God. That goes even into childbirth: there is much our people don't know about it. Most brothers don't know what to do for a wife after she gives birth. The sisters are destroyed, and their husbands are destroyed too, so solutions have to be given to the men.

That is why the class will not use Esau's term postpartum depression, which comes with a negative stigma. Call it postpartum difficulties, or the days of her purification.

“Because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children.” God rejects a people that rejects his knowledge.
“As they were increased, so they sinned against me”: as our people increased, we sinned against God. “Therefore will I change their glory into shame.”

“They eat up the sin of my people, and they set their heart on their iniquity.” The heart is the mind. To set your heart on your iniquity is to not want to change: you hear the scriptures come forth and you would rather stay stuck the way you are. It was the same with our people then as it is today.

“Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me.” Everybody among us says they love the Lord and gives him praise with the mouth.

“But have removed their heart far from me.” Some brothers, and some liberal-minded, broken-minded sisters among us, have hearts far from God. They hear the word online every Saturday, and they do nothing with it. They keep the liberal way of thinking and don't want to change.

“And their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men.” Which man taught you? The white man. He taught you education and medical education. Everything we know was taught to us by our oppressor, our enemy. On the eugenics tree Esau used education, psychology, biology, history, mental testing, statistics, politics, economics and biography to destroy us. None of it was taught for our benefit. It was taught to keep you in a destroyed state of mind, and to keep you divided against your husband, against your man.

It is our job to change those minds and restore the broken minds of the sisters, and if they hate the Deacon for it, so be it.

“Surely your turning of things upside down shall be esteemed as the potter’s clay.” Esau turned everything upside down, but God will esteem it as the potter's clay and turn it back the way it is supposed to be.

The Lord does not just come down and do it. It is up to the men the Lord sent on the earth to change things back. Our sisters' minds are broken, and our brothers' minds are broken. We were taught lies, and it is our job to bring the people out of the lies they were taught in slavery and out of the slave mentality.

“Now go, write it before them in a table, and note it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever: That this is a rebellious people.” God already let us know his people are rebellious. So when the word is heard and people get mad, they are not mad at the Deacon; they are mad at the Lord.

“Lying children”: you love lies, the white man's lies. “Children that will not hear the law of the Lord”: you don't want to hear it; you want to stay in your liberal way of thinking.

“Which say to the seers, See not.” The Deacon is a seer and can see what is happening. Last week's lesson showed the broken state of some sisters, and they started bugging, because they don't want to be shown what the seer sees.

“And to the prophets, Prophesy not unto us right things.” The right thing is that the sisters have to change the way they think. That is not hatred; it is love.

“Speak unto us smooth things.” Nobody wants to hear: you're dealing with depression, so fight it, overcome it, and stop using it as an excuse. That is the real thing, and the people will not get smooth things from the seers; that would be doing them a disservice. Nor will the prophets “prophesy deceits.”

So when these scriptures come out, examine yourself. If you fit anything in them, just fix it. Don't turn into an enemy because the word of God cuts you.

“Because ye despise this word”: our people hate the word of God. “And trust in oppression and perverseness”: you trust everything the white man taught you, and that is the oppression. “And stay thereon”: you want to stay there and maintain the state of this world, an independent woman, a liberal woman, and not change.
“Therefore this iniquity shall be to you as a breach ready to fall.” When the Lord comes, he is going to destroy it.

“Happy art thou, O Israel: who is like unto thee, O people saved by the Lord, the shield of thy help, and who is the sword of thy excellency! and thine enemies shall be found liars unto thee.” Everything that was taught to us is lies. It is hard to hear, brothers and sisters, but we can't pick some things and hold on to some things. Everything we were taught was meant to destroy us.

Many of the terms we learned in America don't exist in other countries. Ask a brother raised in Jamaica whether the women there spoke of postpartum depression after having children: it did not exist there, nor ADHD, nor in Haiti. The eugenics trees from Esau's meetings of 1912 to 1932 show how deep he went, in his studies of race and in how to control our people. The Willie Lynch letter says to take the female and test her in every way, because she is the most important factor for good economics. Esau understands that the Israelite woman is the most important factor, and what he wants is for our sisters to believe him over the Bible.

Postpartum is in the Bible. All through history sisters have dealt with postpartum difficulties: the sickness does not end at the birth, some are hospitalized, and some even die. But Esau added depression to it for psychological reasons, and to sell medication: when you are diagnosed with it, you are handed antidepressant pills. Be very mindful of that terminology.

“And be not conformed to this world”: brothers and sisters, we cannot be conformed to this world.

“But be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind.” Our minds need renewing because our enemies lied to us and we are destroyed for lack of knowledge. To renew your mind is to acknowledge that everything you were taught was lies, and to be taught all over again, like a little child, instead of going by what you think and feel. This truth is about change. The liberal sisters who got upset at last week's lesson only have to change. Their minds are broken, and that is what the teaching is here for: to help them.

This world teaches you that you don't have to have kids: finish college, build a career, establish yourself, have kids at forty, freeze your eggs. Liberal women push it on the sisters: childbirth is painful and life-threatening, and I don't want to risk my life having kids. Sisters, be very mindful of what you allow to enter into you, because it can defile you.

“Notwithstanding she shall be saved in childbearing, if they continue in faith and charity and holiness with sobriety.” This does not mean a woman just has to have babies and she gets the kingdom. Childbearing reaches into all that God requires of a wife, things the sisters will never hear from liberal women. And she must continue in faith, which is believing this truth, and in charity and holiness.

precepts.why:
Here is what it means to be saved in childbearing. “I will therefore that the younger women marry”: get married, sisters, and stop saying you're not getting married. The childbearing reaches into being a good wife.

“Bear children”: part of being a good wife is having children. Don't hate children. “Guide the house”: take care of your house, the cooking and the cleaning. To be saved in childbearing is to be a good support to your husband and a good wife, with charity and with faith in this truth.

“Give none occasion to the adversary to speak reproachfully.” The sisters among us are supposed to be a light to the world. So how can any of them support Lindsay Clancy, a white woman who murdered her three children? She was never diagnosed with postpartum depression or postpartum psychosis, and she tried to use it to get away with murder; she wanted out of the life of being a mother. Any sister among us who supports her, who says I understand what she went through, is evil as hell, and the same sisters will turn on us down the line. The Deacon is not bending for any of them: they have to change their minds, and the Lord commands us to set our face against the daughters of his people because they follow foolishness like that.

Liberal women use postpartum depression as a license to hate their kids, to refuse to have kids, to hate their husbands and refuse them, even to kill their children. Sisters do go through real things after birth, and a sister with no support system, or with an abusive husband, can fall into depression. But women among us who deal with mental issues have solutions, and none of it gives a sister license to be evil.

Everything read here goes back to “she shall be saved in childbearing.” “Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception.” Her sorrow starts at thirteen or fourteen, when her menstrual cycle begins, because that has to do with her eggs and her conception, and she starts feeling pain.

“In sorrow thou shalt bring forth children.” The sorrow runs from the first cycle to the pregnancy, through the morning sickness and the throwing up, into the birth itself, and on after the birth. Sisters, the reason you go through all this pain and sorrow is the evil your mother Eve did in the beginning.

“And thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.” So to be saved in childbearing is to respect and honour your husband, and have kids.

sense.text: This is the sorrow of childbearing. “Rachel travailed, and she had hard labour”: her labour was very hard. “The midwife said unto her, Fear not; thou shalt have this son also.”

“And it came to pass, as her soul was in departing, (for she died).” Rachel died giving birth. The seriousness of giving birth is understood here: the Deacon's wife carried four high-risk pregnancies, on bedrest for months, cut badly by the doctors. With the last child, Benji, Esau's doctors saw some abnormality and pushed the choice of killing the baby; the Deacon said to hell with them and trusted in the Lord. Esau's medical system is set up to destroy. His son Ezekiel was born premature. So nobody can say he doesn't understand what women go through.

“She called his name Ben–oni”, which means son of my sorrow. She went through so much sorrow in that birth that she died. “But his father called him Benjamin”, son of the right hand. Jacob was not ruled by emotion over his wife's dying words; he would not name his son after sorrow.

It shows that women go through great sorrows in childbirth, and some die. And that judgment is for what Eve did in the beginning, which many daughters follow in Eve's footsteps and do today.

Rachel's death after giving birth has a spiritual side. “And when Rachel saw that she bare Jacob no children, Rachel envied her sister.” Our mother Rachel was rebellious; she worshipped idols, and she was very pretty, more favoured than Leah. Good-looking women have issues, and they will use their beauty to control some brothers. Jacob loved Rachel, but Rachel wasn't right.

“And said unto Jacob, Give me children, or else I die.” Rachel was dealing with depression because she couldn't have kids, and she tried to manipulate her husband: give me kids, lest I kill myself. That is a demon.

And what happened to her? God gave her a baby, and she died. Sometimes the Lord judges you on the very things you speak. That is why the sisters are warned again and again: be careful what you call to yourself, and be careful of throwing that depression talk around, because if you put it out there you will become depressed. Esau understands that psychology.

“And Jacob’s anger was kindled against Rachel: and he said, Am I in God’s stead, who hath withheld from thee the fruit of the womb?” Jacob was angry. Woman, am I God? God has shut up your womb. It isn't me, for I am having children; something isn't right with you.
“Behold my maid Bilhah, go in unto her; and she shall bear upon my knees, that I may also have children by her.” Bilhah was her handmaid.

precepts.why:
“For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.” You can call judgment on yourself. Rachel, envious of her sister and depressed, argued with her husband and told him, give me a baby or I'm going to kill myself. In time the Lord gave her a second child, and she died, as if the Lord said: I'm tired of you.

Be careful of the words you say and the things you call to yourself.

“My son, attend to my words; incline thine ear unto my sayings. Let them not depart from thine eyes; keep them in the midst of thine heart.” Keep the laws of God in your heart, in your mind. “For they are life unto those that find them, and health to all their flesh.”

“Keep thy heart with all diligence.” Your heart is your mind. You are not supposed to sit there saying I hate myself, I hate my husband, I hate my kids. When those thoughts come, shake them off. Don't let a brother you can't stand fill your mind with evil thoughts either. Sisters are not supposed to be home depressed. Does it happen after birth? Yes. But when it happens, get help; the leaders are there to help. Postpartum difficulties are not to be used as a weapon against your husband and your kids, as so many women use them.

“For out of it are the issues of life.”

“Put away from thee a froward mouth, and perverse lips put far from thee.” Rachel had a froward mouth. She said she would die if she wasn't given a baby, and God answered her. Be careful of the things you say.

sense.text:
“For as he thinketh in his heart, so is he.” If you don't keep your heart, and you dwell on anger, envy or depression, it will manifest itself. Esau understands this too; that is why he pushes certain things through the rap music, because what people take in shapes their behaviour.

So if a sister goes through difficulties after birth and keeps saying I'm depressed, she will become depressed. It does happen. But when those thoughts come, shake them off and don't entertain them. When the Deacon's wife came to him years ago saying she felt down and depressed, he told her: that's the devil, shake it off. He sat down with her and went through the scriptures, and then told her to go find something to do. A man cannot just let his wife sit in the house depressed and evil, and use it as an excuse.

Women can become depressed after postpartum difficulties, and it is the husband's job to help guide her mind against these things. Esau understood this verse in his psychology; that is why he came up with the term postpartum depression. He keeps telling you that you're depressed until you believe it. Sisters, shake that spirit.

“Give not over thy mind to heaviness.” God says don't give your mind over to it, and the Deacon will not entertain that spirit. Life is hard sometimes. Things hit everybody at once, and even the Deacon feels that heaviness trying to jump on him, but we have to shake it off and not allow depression to rise up on us. Stay away from someone depressed all the time, because spirits jump. Saying it over and over and believing it is giving your mind over to heaviness.

“And afflict not thyself in thine own counsel.” In your own thoughts you afflict yourself. It happens with sisters after they give birth: they start afflicting themselves in their minds. Brothers have to be able to spot it and help them.

“The gladness of the heart is the life of man.” That is your medicine. You have to be glad in your heart and fight that spirit, not let it overcome you. “And the joyfulness of a man prolongeth his days.”

“Love thine own soul, and comfort thy heart.” You must learn to comfort your own heart. And brothers must comfort their wives' hearts too: in postpartum difficulties, and in general, when she is overwhelmed by life and feels down even when it has nothing to do with the kids.

“Remove sorrow far from thee: for sorrow hath killed many.” Many have gone crazy and been destroyed through sorrow. The sisters get the same word the Deacon gave his wife: fix it, it's Satan, shake it off, and he will help you. Satan is riding you, and you have to shake him off.

“And there is no profit therein.” But Esau sees profit in it: if you are sorrowful, he can sell you medication for it. It is big business: keep telling the black woman she is depressed, she will become depressed, and money will be made off her.

Most of what is listed under postpartum depression is what women deal with naturally after birth. But two things Esau put on that list are a no: thinking about killing yourself, and thinking about killing your baby. Only someone with underlying mental illness thinks like that. Birth can cause it, but that is rare, and the women heard talking like that today are women who hate their kids.

precepts.why:
“A merry heart doeth good like a medicine.” A merry heart heals you like medicine, the same as the gladness of heart that is the life of man. That is why sisters should not be running around saying they're depressed.

“But a broken spirit drieth the bones.” A broken spirit, a broken mind, makes you sick, and it can even bring on mental illness.

“Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared: for this day is holy unto our Lord: neither be ye sorry; for the joy of the Lord is your strength.” You must have joy in serving God; that is where strength comes from. To be depressed all the time is to have no joy in the Lord. Even a sister struggling with postpartum difficulties has to find joy, something she loves doing, and come up out of it, not sit in the house saying woe is me.

If there is a crowd of depressed, melancholy sisters among us, the leaders are doing a bad job as leaders and the husbands a bad job as husbands. But there is Hope and Healing, a programme for those with mental illness, with psychiatrists who went to school for it and bring the scriptures into what they learned in Esau's system. There is Birth of a Nation too. A sister gave birth in Jersey that week with only her husband there, who doesn't know the medical terms, and that should never happen: there should be sisters, doulas and midwives, a support system so she doesn't feel alone, and sisters cooking and bringing food after the baby comes. The young sisters are needed to learn herbs, Esau's medicine, and how to deliver children. So there is no excuse, and instead of hating the Deacon for hitting a nerve, the sisters can work together and take it to another level.

sense.text: “Where there is no vision, the people perish.” This is not a congregation without vision. The Bishops have vision: they saw these things were needed and set up the programmes. Where there is no vision, people start dealing with depression and difficulties after birth with nobody to help them. The leaders see what the nation needs and what the sisters need, and they are trying to bring that message to the people.

precepts.why:
“These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself: but I will reprove thee.” Esau is being reproved right now.

“And set them in order before thine eyes.” The vision is to set our people in order. That order is the structure of the household, the man at the head, then the woman, then the children. But it is also our own schools teaching our children, our own doctors and our own medical teams. These are already set up in the schools; now the support system for the sisters has to be much stronger, especially on the east coast. Love your neighbour as yourself, and make sure that when a sister gives birth, the husband is not there alone, but people who know these things are there to help.

When the Deacon was young and had his first child, he didn't know these things, or he would never have let the doctors do what they did to his wife: they cut her so that she could only have a few children. That is warfare. The Black Panthers had their own clinics, and we have to come to that level. So the young sisters should go to school and learn these skills to help their nation, because terrible times are coming, and they are the ones who will bring forth the young prophets who will be born in the earth.

sense.text:
Brothers are destroyed too: before, the midwives dealt with the women and they were separated from the men, and today many brothers don't know how to deal with a wife after she has a baby, so they get frustrated. Here is a solution.

“When a man hath taken a new wife, he shall not go out to war, neither shall he be charged with any business: but he shall be free at home one year, and shall cheer up his wife which he hath taken.” Many a wife is down because her husband doesn't cheer her up. This law is a way of helping with postpartum difficulties. Cheering her up covers a lot: first, giving her a baby, and the act of giving it to her. Then, when she gets pregnant and goes through the postpartum difficulties, cheering her up is still the husband's job.

After the eighty days for his child Zion were done, the Deacon left the kids with Deacon Malachi and his wife in Brooklyn for a couple of days, made a plan, took his wife to the Poconos, and cheered her up. A brother can take his wife out from time to time. He can help with whatever he can, even if he can't cook, because today we no longer have the big family support system of grandmothers and sisters coming by. Often it is just you and your wife, and that time is very straining on the sisters. Women feel down sometimes, and their bodies change too.

precepts.why:
“Isaac was sporting with Rebekah his wife.” Sporting means to laugh, play, caress or revel. The way Isaac was dealing and playing with her, Abimelech could tell she was not his sister, because a brother and sister don't act like that.

It is fine for a brother to sport with his wife. It helps take away the sorrows and the difficulties after she comes out of her purification. Laugh with your wife in the house; take her out, walk with her hand in hand with your arm around her, and show her off. It is fine to hold your wife's hand. That is cheering her up.

She trusts what her husband says, so when she asks if she is fat after giving birth, don't tear her down. The key thing is that you have to cheer your wife up after she comes out of labour: take her someplace nice, because pushing out that baby was very hard. In a healthy marriage the sisters should not be talking depression at all, but many brothers don't know these things, and it causes problems. These things are hard to learn, and they are being taught as they are learned.

“Husbands, love your wives, and be not bitter against them.” After a birth there are ways a brother can end up bitter against his wife. The intimacy diminishes, and the baby is always crying, every time he wants to be with her. A sister may not want to get pregnant again right away; whatever a husband and wife work out about that is between them. Some women can have children back to back, but a woman's womb needs time to heal.

Kids change a marriage. Things are not like when it was just the two of you; now it is about growth, starting a family. These postpartum difficulties are for the brothers to learn to navigate, deal with and overcome, without becoming bitter.

“Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity.” To prevent difficulties like postpartum, be joyful with the woman you have. After she gives birth, don't neglect her and leave her there. Cheer her up, make sure she gets the right foods, and make sure she is not in the house by herself all the time, because that alone can be depressing. Sometimes take the kids to somebody and let them watch them a while, or she can become overwhelmed, and even that can bring on a form of depression.

Understand too the emotional outbursts. The Deacon came home once to find his wife, eight and a half months pregnant, up a ladder painting the kitchen to get it ready before the baby came. He yelled at her, what the hell is wrong with you, man, get off the damn ladder, and she cried: she was only trying to get the kitchen ready before the baby came. You can't have paint around a baby. Still, a man has to be patient, say sorry for yelling, and learn from these things. Women go through hormonal changes, but the sisters can't use their hormones as an excuse to be evil and disrespectful. It is the brothers' job to cheer their wives up.

sense.text:
Mental illness is real. Some brothers and sisters among us have anxiety disorder, schizophrenia, or bipolar disorder. But look at what God calls mental illness, and be careful of the things you call on yourself.

“The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart.” Madness is a curse God smites us with. Astonishment of heart is a deep, paralysing state of mental confusion, panic and bewilderment, an affliction of the inner life, a person's thoughts, emotions and will. It is the mind that is not right, as when Nebuchadnezzar lost his mind. That is the bipolar and the schizophrenia: a broken mind. A lot of worrying brings on that sickness.

precepts.why: “They brought unto him all sick people that were taken with divers diseases and torments, and those which were possessed with devils, and those which were lunatick, and those that had the palsy.” All the sick came to Christ. What Esau calls mental illness today, the bipolar and the schizophrenia, is devils. The palsy is understood here as autism. All these things we read of are unclean spirits, demon possession.

“Lord, have mercy on my son: for he is lunatick.” Lunatick means moonstruck, affected by the moon, and was used for seizures and severe mental conditions: a sickness of the mind, a broken mind. The Bible calls it lunatick: he was crazy.

“And sore vexed: for ofttimes he falleth into the fire, and oft into the water.” He kept throwing himself into fire and water to kill himself. That is what the lunatick spirit does: it makes you want to kill yourself. Should sisters be talking about wanting to kill themselves, or the baby, after they give birth? That is a lunatick spirit, a devil.

“And I brought him to thy disciples, and they could not cure him.” Christ answered, “O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you? how long shall I suffer you?” He was talking to his disciples. “And Jesus rebuked the devil; and he departed out of him: and the child was cured from that very hour.” That lunatick spirit was a devil. Talk about wanting to kill yourself and kill people is a lunatick spirit in you: you lost your damn mind. It's a demon. Every demon that inhabits a person is trying to destroy them, to kill them.

“Why could not we cast him out?” “Because of your unbelief.” The disciples' faith was weak at that time and they had not been built up yet; later they were casting out demons everywhere, and even Peter's shadow healed people. “If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you.”

“Howbeit this kind goeth not out but by prayer and fasting.” There are levels to demons. Envy, jealousy, murder and adultery are demons. But the lunatick demon, the one that controls your mind and your thoughts and makes you want to hurt yourself and others, is a high-level demon. Why call that to yourself by saying you have postpartum depression and want to kill yourself and your kid? Remember the woman in Tobit: every man who married her was killed. The demon did not just float around; it controlled her, and she had no recollection of it, the same way the demon jumped on the men who tried to cast out devils in the name of Christ and beat them. If you feel depressed, shake it off; don't entertain that demon, because it is hard to shake.

The Pharisees said Christ's disciples weren't fasting and praying like John's, and Christ said they would when he left. After he died, they gave themselves to prayer and fasting continually, and you can see their growth. Men will rise up among us who will heal the lunatick, autism and seizures by the power of the Holy Spirit, not the bull crap seen on television. When the Deacon's son Ezekiel had seizures at seven, the Deacon threw the medication away and fasted and prayed, and the boy never had another; but that was his faith, and he is not telling anyone to stop their medication. Prayer and fasting build up the Holy Spirit in you. When his own spirit feels drained and down, he knows it is Satan, and he fasts and prays to renew his spirit.

sense.text:
“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted.” The brokenhearted are the mentally ill of our people, those whose minds are broken. Christ healed the child who kept trying to kill himself; today they call it a disease, but then it was called what it is: a demon. You can't see it, but it is a demon.

A lot of sisters' minds are broken, maybe not schizophrenia crazy or bipolar crazy, but crazy in the way they think and move. Look at how sisters in society sleep with man after man. When a woman sleeps around, energy is transferred and she is joined to whatever demons those men carry; that is another thing that creates bipolar in women. Some sisters came in good while single and went crazy as soon as they married. A sister who has been with a hundred guys is broken; some sisters need to stay single and serve God the rest of their lives instead of defiling a brother.

Liberal sisters have crept in unawares with liberal thoughts, waiting to trick one of the sucker brothers, marry him and mess his life up. One sister, once a lesbian, was among us five years and seemed changed; after she married and had the baby she hated her husband and the baby, said this was not what she wanted, and went back to being a lesbian. Those who relate to Lindsay Clancy's pain have demons on them. Anyone offended by last week's lesson should leave: it never said postpartum is not in the scriptures or that women don't deal with it; it said it is wrong to use it to justify evil.

Our people's minds are broken, the men's and the women's, but much more so the women's, because they are the weaker vessel. As the men get themselves together, it is their job to get these damn women together. If the men have to change, the women have to change.

“To preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind.” The blind are our people, who can't see.

precepts.why:
“The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart: And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways.” Everything Christ came to heal is in Deuteronomy 28.

The brokenhearted of Luke 4:18 are the madness of Deuteronomy 28:28. The recovering of sight to the blind is the blindness: the Lord smote us with blindness, so we cannot see clearly, because we were taught lies.

“He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.” IUIC is a place of healing. Brothers have to be healed, and sisters have to be healed, from all the mental issues we carry.

Those among us dealing with mental illness are told straight: don't get off your medication if your faith is not there, and anyone who comes around acting crazy will be put out of the school. But the Deacon saw a brother lose his mind, hearing and seeing things and chased by the police, and when the Bishop said he was bat crap crazy, the Deacon said we're going to heal him. The brother fasted five days and prayed, and today you would never know he was crazy. People said to take him to the mad house and put him on medication; God healed him instead.

A broken heart means something is broken in your mind: demons controlling the mind, a spirit talking to you and making you want to hurt people. Not everyone has the same level of faith, so stay on your medication until the leaders come to that power and get the demon off of you.

“For it was neither herb, nor mollifying plaister, that restored them to health: but thy word, O Lord, which healeth all things.” It was neither herbs nor plaister that healed them, but the word of God. Do you believe the word of God heals all things? All things means all things. The Deacon saw a person with mental illness, a broken heart, healed by God so that you would never know.

So none of the sisters among us should be saying I'm depressed, I want to kill myself, calling things on themselves. God's word heals all things. This is a place of healing, not a place to use postpartum difficulties to be evil.

“A woman, which was diseased with an issue of blood twelve years, came behind him, and touched the hem of his garment.” She had been bleeding twelve years straight. “For she said within herself, If I may but touch his garment, I shall be whole.” And Christ said, “Daughter, be of good comfort; thy faith hath made thee whole.”

What heals you is God's word, but you can't just say God's word is going to heal me without believing it. The power is in believing, having faith that God's word can heal you. Sisters, get your minds right, and let's build this nation.
